Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Systematix Group. As a reminder, all participant line will be in the 
listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by 
pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being 
recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Siddharth Rajpurohit from Systematix Group. Thank you, 
and over to you, sir. 
Siddharth Rajpurohit: 
Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining Bank of Maharashtra's Q2 FY27 Post Results 
Earnings Call. From the management today, we have Mr. Nidhu Saxena, the MD and CEO of 
the bank. We thank the management for giving us the opportunity to host the call and 
congratulate on the strong numbers. 
 
I hand over the call now to Mr. Saxena for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Nidhu Saxena: 
Thank you, and good evening to one and all, and thank you for joining this investor call. The 
business and the numbers for this quarter has been quite encouraging for the bank. We had set 
out the year with a set of guidance numbers across all metrics of growth, profitability, asset 
quality, capital adequacy and so on. 
 
And I'm happy to share that each one of those guidance numbers have been met, and this is 
getting consistently met also is one good feature. I will quickly take you through the highlights. 
The business for this September '26 has grown by 25%, within which advances have grown at 
the rate of 30% Y-o-Y. 
 
A large contribution -- significant contribution has come from the IBU and minus the IBU, also, 
the credit growth in the bank Y-o-Y has been healthy 23%. So all verticals of the RAM, Retail, 
Agri, MSME, have grown individually and have grown more than 20%. The large credit growth, 
which is seen, is also Y-o-Y growth of 38%. 
 
So INR36,000 crores of large credit has grown Y-o-Y. And as I just said, 50%, INR18,000 crores 
of this has happened in the GIFT City IBU branch of the bank. The rest INR18,000 crores has 
happened in the domestic large credit, which is again a healthy 19% growth. 
 
As against the domestic credit growth of 23%, the deposits have also grown healthy 22% Y-o-
Y. So even if we exclude the FCNR (B), the deposit growth has happened at the Y-o-Y rate of 
19% within which CASA has grown in the bank at 12% Y-o-Y and bank has added in absolute 
terms, INR19,000 crores of CASA over the last FY. 
 
GNPA also has improved. It has reduced by 47 basis points and GNPA stands at 1.25%. 
Likewise, NNPA also reduction by 6 basis points. NNPA for the bank is at 0.12%. Provision 
coverage ratio is at a healthy level of 98.53%. Stress in the loan book also has been well 
managed.

It has also reduced overall 167 bps year-on-year from 4.93% to 3.26%, within which the SMA 
1 and 2 portfolio is also shown a reduction of 50 basis points, and it stands at 1.37%. And we 
have seen the improvement in the stress levels across the sectors, Retail, Agriculture, MSME, 
every sector has registered an improvement. 
 
Above INR5 crores, the NPA -- the stress is near 0.13%. And exclude one state account, it is 
only 0.11%, which also has improved 4 basis points. The cost of deposits and overall cost, we 
have been able to manage and maintain well. We have been exercising the various options of 
availing refinance raising through infra bonds from time to time. 
 
Today, in the bank, we have an outstanding of INR18,300 crores of refinance book, which is 
between 6% to 6.5%. Likewise, infra bond raises, which happened in the last FY, outstanding is 
INR2,400 crores. 
 
These have been also supporting the credit growth at reasonable and able to give reasonable 
profitability levels to the bank. So cost of deposits also has reduced for the bank year-on-year 
by 4 basis points, stands at 4.38%. Likewise, cost of funds overall have reduction -- shown 
reduction of 25 basis points. It stands at 4.07%. So with slippages also staying under check, 
profitability for the bank has been good. 
 
Operating profit has shown a growth of 31% Y-o-Y, while the net profit has grown year-on-year 
41%. As a result of this, the ROE has shown a sharp improvement. ROE has improved by 440 
basis points and has reached 27%, 26.98%, to be precise. 
 
NIM has improved by 12 basis points to 3.97%. And the ROA has improved by 20 basis points 
to 2.02%. The capital adequacy is also maintained at the healthy level and above our guidance 
number. CET1 is 15.61% and CRAR stands at 18.51%. Bank is maintaining a good LCR. The 
LCR is standing at 123% and NSFR at 127%. 
 
So this is overall highlight from my side. I think we should take some questions from the 
investors.

fact, you have reached many of the milestones. The business for the first time, I think, has 
crossed INR7 lakh crores, if I'm not wrong. Credit is also more than INR3 lakh -- crossed INR3 
lakh crores. 
 
Your EPS for the first time has gone above INR3. ROA is above 2% and many, many more such 
milestones and the records which you have created in this quarter and the half year. 
Congratulations for that, sir.

last quarter. 
 
But at the same time, in the contingency side, which was for the COVID-19, we are gradually 
reducing our provision from INR1,200 crores to now in 3, 4 quarters coming down to INR510 
crores. Coupled with that, the ECL provisioning, which is required to be done, all these 3 
questions must be having only one answer from your side. What is our ECL preparedness? How 
much do we need to provide? And how are we prepared for it, sir? 
Nidhu Saxena: 
Thank you, Mr. Ajmera. I think you have covered the top line also issue. Let me confirm that,

which is provisions. 
 
So I will just like to highlight that provisions for NPAs and provisions for standard, I'll give you 
the number. The NPA provisions September '25 quarter last year, June '26, that is the Q1 of this 
FY and September '26, the current quarter we are discussing, the number, you must have seen 
reduced number. 
 
So INR580 crores has come down to INR120 crores. So there are 2 broad reasons around this. 
One is that with the high provision coverage ratio, we are maintaining of 98.5% plus. Our 
incremental requirement that comes every quarter for providing for NPAs is a very nominal 
amount. This particular quarter, also, we have experienced good recovery in the Q2. 
 
And even the upgradation number has been good. Yes, there is a support also from the -- some 
recoveries in the debt waiver has come because that book also was 100%. I mean, we were 
holding with 98.5% provision, we were holding -- it was almost 100% provided for book and 
whatever recovery has come also has aided towards that. So net, this is one reason that this 
provision for NPA requirement has got reduced, and this is how it is. 
 
Second, the standard provision book, if you see INR158 crores was last year. This year was 
INR603 crores. So this is on account of ECL provisioning that we have done of INR500 crores. 
So that's how in the standard assets, you are seeing that provisioning has increased -- number 
has increased from INR150 crores to INR600 crores. 
 
And in terms of ECL provisioning requirements, we had our assessments done way back when 
the draft guidelines were under discussion. And INR250 crores upfront front ending, we had 
already done previously for ECL. This quarter, we have done INR500 crores. 
 
Our total assessment was that INR2,500 crores is our ECL provisioning to be done in 4 years. 
Yes, we have put some system in place and validation is going on. Maybe this number appears 
to even go down. 
 
But assuming INR2,500 crores, today with INR250 crores plus INR500 crores in this quarter, 
INR750 crores of ECL provisioning that we have already done, this is covering more than 1 year

And along with that, this recovery also from the written-off account, which has been

So, Ajmera-ji, let me take FCNR. First, we had a mobilization of $820 million and $760 million 
was IBU loan where the leverage from the IBU is $560 million only. So INR7,800 crores, 
INR8,000 crores of FCNR (B). And so this is what has actually gone into the IBU overall book 
of INR18,500 crores, $560 million of leverage from the FCNR thing. So going forward, yes, this 
window is not there. 
 
But coming on the domestic side, I have the guidance number of 18%, and we are -- other than 
IBU, we have grown 23%. So if you see individually, all verticals have grown at 20% plus. And 
even the large credit is showing a robust growth. It has grown Y-o-Y 19%. In terms of credit 
pipeline that I'm holding, currently, we have INR23,000 crores of proposals in pipeline. And up 
to March '27, we have estimated INR10,000 crores out of this will be getting disbursed. 
 
Sectors where we have taken exposure and where these proposals of INR23,000 crores lie are 
mostly infra -- within infra, infra power, around 18%, infra road, HAM projects of NHAI and 
12%, renewable energy, 10%, and metal and other space, 10%. We are doing niche segments 
like data centers and other things which are actually the growth opportunities available to banks. 
 
So this is how -- plus annually, you might have recall, you can recall 200 branches annually we 
are opening. So in the segment of Retail and MSME business, fresh business is getting added 
through these branches as and when they are opening in the bank. In this half year, we have 
made 77 branches functional. 
 
So whatever branches -- these business branches are -- new branches are getting is also 
ultimately adding to the growth, both credit side, deposit side. So I don't see a challenge at all to 
maintain a pace above our guidance of 18% in credit in future also.

Nidhu Saxena: 
So if you see Y-o-Y basis, we have seen a reduction. But if you ask me, we have been very 
mindful of doing business and doing business profitably. We have been very consciously looking 
at alternate sources of raising our resources, whether it is through the refinance window, whether 
it is through raising infra bonds. 
 
Whether it is through capitalizing on our strong investor engagement and going for debt 
issuances, whether it -- for the bank in its 92 years of lifetime, this was the first time that we 
took assessment, which is around $2 billion is what we had in mind is what we can have an 
appetite for raising through the RBI swap windows for OFCBs and FCNR (B). 
 
And we decided to do around $1.5 billion. I can tell you that we did $1.65 billion, putting FCNR 
(B) and OFCB together. And there also, we are going to get the rate advantage in this scenario 
of interest rates going up, both domestic and global markets. I think the MTN program where 
we raised -- it was the first ever foreign bond issuance for the bank, and we got 3x the issue size 
as subscription from the investors. And at a very good rate, it was very well timed.

place, some ballpark numbers as to what in terms of profitability, this one initiative of 
fundraising through foreign bonds will lead to the bank. 
 
So those numbers also are there. And I think -- so the point is we have been very cautious. If we 
have done a lot of FCNR (B), some high-cost bulk deposits, we have consciously allowed to 
leave the system and focus more on low-cost components of the deposits.
